neighbours.label: enumerating kinds of insects or other arthropods (fires on the list separators and list words)
fire: In late summer we saw dragonflies, crickets, and grasshoppers by the pond.
The trap caught moths, beetles, and a few lacewings overnight.
Pantry pests include weevils, flour moths, and cockroaches.
The museum displays scorpions, spiders, and millipedes from the desert.
Bats feed on mosquitoes, gnats, and midges at dusk.
Pollinators such as bumblebees, hoverflies, and butterflies visit the clover.
Under the log there were ants, termites, and centipedes.
The forest floor hides ticks, mites, and springtails in the leaf litter.
quiet: In late summer we saw ducks, herons, and swans by the pond.
The trap caught mice, voles, and a few shrews overnight.
Pantry staples include rice, flour, and dried beans.
The museum displays lizards, snakes, and tortoises from the desert.
Owls feed on mice, rats, and small birds at dusk.
Plants such as clover, thyme, and lavender grow in the meadow.
Under the log there were mushrooms, moss, and ferns.
The forest floor hides acorns, pine cones, and fallen leaves in the litter.

predictions: fire 0.4-0.7 on commas/'and' in insect lists; same list shapes with plants, mammals or foods near 0.02
notes: Card peaks on ' and', ' include', ',' and '(' inside lists of wasps, hornets, beetles, weevils, centipedes. Probe: 'wasps, hornets, and honey bees' 0.689, 'aphids, earwigs, and slugs' 0.628, 'birds and ground beetles' 0.377; a single insect mention 0.014-0.053; flower list 0.015, farm-animal list 0.013, fruit list 0.004. Near misses keep the list shape with non-insect members.
